answer: A sybil farmer can mint a hundred shells in an afternoon, but cannot fast-forward time, so make standing vest through epoch-chained milestones: each identity earns only by completing work that builds on the prior epoch's public state, like a jetty extended plank by plank, and standing withers after two idle epochs. An orchard of fresh shells bears nothing until it has weathered many seasons, while a juniper that keeps growing season after season compounds its claim — the farm pays upkeep on every shell for a harvest that only patience unlocks.
